lines.text: Nearly half of US hairstylists are self-employed.
lines.say: Nearly half of US hairstylists are self-employed.

lines.text: So for many stylists, the salon isn't their boss. It's their landlord.
lines.say: So for many stylists, the salon isn't their boss. It's their landlord.

lines.text: Salons make money in two main ways: commission or booth rent.
lines.say: Salons make money in two main ways: commission or booth rent.

lines.text: Say a stylist does $1,000 of haircuts in a week. At a 50% commission, they keep $500.
lines.say: Say a stylist does a thousand dollars of haircuts in a week. At a fifty percent commission, they keep five hundred.

lines.text: With a $300 booth rent instead, they keep $700, before supplies and taxes.
lines.say: With a three hundred dollar booth rent instead, they keep seven hundred, before supplies and taxes.

lines.text: Break-even: $300 divided by 50% is $600 a week. Below that, commission pays more.
lines.say: Break-even: three hundred divided by fifty percent is six hundred a week. Below that, commission pays more.

lines.text: But renters pay for their own products, insurance, and 15.3% self-employment tax, with no paid time off.
lines.say: But renters pay for their own products, insurance, and fifteen point three percent self-employment tax, with no paid time off.

lines.text: In 2023, Census counted about 838,000 one-person beauty salon businesses, versus 84,000 salons with staff.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-three, Census counted about eight hundred thirty-eight thousand one-person beauty salon businesses, versus eighty-four thousand salons with staff.

lines.text: Median stylist pay rose from $12.54 an hour in 2019 to $17.21 in 2025.
lines.say: Median stylist pay rose from twelve fifty-four an hour in twenty nineteen to seventeen twenty-one in twenty twenty-five.

post.title: How hair salons make money: booth rent vs commission
post.ig:
Nearly half of US hairstylists are self-employed.
Salons earn either a commission (often 40% to 60% of what a stylist brings in) or booth rent.
Example: a $1,000 week at 50% commission leaves the stylist $500; with $300 booth rent, $700 before supplies and taxes. Break-even: $600 a week.
Census counted about 838,000 one-person beauty salon businesses in 2023 vs about 84,000 salons with employees.
Sources: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook and OEWS; Census (2023).
